subject: Axes on both sides of a graph

messages.author: 4d997d9a2ee25f2a
messages.subject: Axes on both sides of a graph
parts:
Hi All,

It seems there is no way to draw axes on both sides of a graph in ggplot.  I know that Hadley has a distaste about putting two different scales on the same graph, but it seems even drawing the same axes twice is not possible.  Cleveland (1994) advocates for tick marks on both Y axes, both on the left and the right.  (Though the labels typically appear only on one side.)  One reason to put tick marks on both sides is so that a person viewing the graph can see the position on the scale of plot symbols that are on the right side of the data frame as well as they can the position on the scale of plot symbols that are on the left side of the data frame.  The grid lines that ggplot uses sometimes visually interfere with the data plots, so I need to use tick marks instead.

So is there any way around to draw axes on both Y axes?

Thanks,
YZ

References

Cleveland, W. S. (1994). The elements of graphing data (revised ed.). Murray Hill, N.J.: AT&T Bell Laboratories.

messages.author: a3c668b849637905
messages.subject: Re: Axes on both sides of a graph
parts:
The width "w" is the sum of two theme elements, by default

axis.ticks.length = unit(0.15, "cm"), and
axis.ticks.margin = unit(0.1,  "cm")

You can subtract unit(0.1,  "cm"), or whatever value your theme defines, and the ticks should touch the panel.
